summary.headline: Turtlemint's first post-listing call: FY26 revenue up 57% to INR 1,098 crores, Q4 first adjusted-EBITDA breakeven quarter (INR 60 crores service EBITDA).
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 platform premium of INR 3,868 crores (up 31% YoY) and operating revenue of INR 1,098 crores (up 57%). Service EBITDA rose 70% to INR 142 crores (about 13% of revenue), and Q4 revenue of INR 357 crores (up 42%) delivered the company's first breakeven quarter at adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis. Corporate overheads fell to 23% of revenue in FY26 from 38% in FY25, and PAT before exceptional items was INR 129 crores. Management declined formal guidance but said FY27 should be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis and that losses or profitability gaps would improve by more than 40%.

segments.name: Insurance distribution (PoSP / Turtlemint Insurance Broking)
segments.commentary: About 97% of FY26 revenue is commission from the broking subsidiary; PoSP premium grew more than 40% in FY26. General insurance is more than 90% of platform premium (revenue split is 90% GI, 10% non-GI per management); health grew more than 60%.

segments.name: Turtlefin (enterprise)
segments.commentary: Enterprise partners (banks, NBFCs, fintechs) contribute about 20% of platform premium, roughly INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic. Take rate is low, transaction-based, and management called it high margin with no direct variable cost.

segments.name: Adjacencies (mutual funds, loans)
segments.commentary: Mutual fund AUM about INR 1,400 crores through the subsidiary; loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised, recently launched. Non-insurance businesses are about 3% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; board decided not to give future guidance, but management gave directional color.
FY27: management expects to reduce losses or improve profitability by more than 40% and to be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis; each quarter expected to exceed the prior one.
FY27 corporate overheads expected to grow with inflation rather than volumes; no exceptional items expected in FY27.

Medium term (about five years / FY30): service EBITDA expected to rise from 13-14% to about 24-25% of revenue, corporate overheads to fall to sub 5-6% of revenue, giving EBITDA/PBT/PAT of about 18-20% of revenue.
Long-run growth framed as continuing the historical 40%-plus CAGR in revenue and key KPIs; dividend policy possible after one to two years of sustained profitability.
capex_capacity: Balance sheet has few fixed assets (IT equipment, offices); no costs are capitalised, all expensed.
Digital partner base: 93,000+ P3M active at 31 March 2026 (51% CAGR over seven years); about 6.5 lakh verified DPs; 46 insurers (45+ partners per Q&A); coverage across 19,000+ PIN codes.
Turtlemint Academy averages 52,000+ monthly active users and 6,500+ training hours per month; certifies over 5,000 new sellers per month.
Insurance Hub gives paperless policy issuance across 40+ insurers; 8 lakh+ quotes generated daily.
Agentic AI and LLM automation under development for support tickets, renewal calling, claims and activation; more updates promised.
demand_pricing: Growth drivers: recruitment of new DPs (about 80% non-insurance background, mostly under 35) plus productivity gains in existing cohorts (frontline premium productivity up 20%+ YoY).

Health insurance growth above 60-75% helped by affordability tailwinds and GST cuts; commissions were cut in Oct-Dec quarter and management says the platform passed these through without slowing volume.
Renewal rates in Q4 were significantly higher than in the same quarter of the prior year; management says renewal rates are above industry averages.
Insurer concentration is low: top 3 insurers about 22% of business; top 100 DPs generated 4.62% of platform premium.
Claims desk settled over INR 85 crores of delayed or rejected claims in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 premium and revenue growth, and is it sustainable given the high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited DP recruitment and productivity, the renewal book, and health tailwinds; H1 growth was flattered by base effects, Q4 growth (about 42%) is closer to steady state, and management expects historical 40%-plus growth to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How would commission regulation changes affect the business, and how are PoSPs classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the asset-light model incurs costs only after a transaction, so commission changes are passed down, as shown in the Oct-Dec GST period. It could not say how the regulator will classify PoSPs as agents or brokers.

qa_highlights.question: How does Turtlemint recruit DPs amid competition, and what is the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of DPs come from non-insurance backgrounds with 60-65 profiles; onboarding is digital plus a pan-India branch network. Management did not quantify TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of the enterprise (Turtlefin) business and its take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise premium is about 20% of platform premium (about INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic). The take rate is low but volume-based and high margin, since tech is already built and licensed; enterprise growth should accelerate as new accounts go live.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal vs new service EBITDA margin, and renewal share?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal service EBITDA margin is about 2.5-3x the new business margin. Renewal revenue is INR 225 crores; management declined to disclose renewal premium.

qa_highlights.question: Non-insurance revenue share and the other financial products?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-insurance is about 3% of FY26 revenue. Mutual fund AUM is about INR 1,400 crores and loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised; the incremental revenue drops straight to service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to the 18-20% long-term EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Service EBITDA is 13-14% today and is expected to reach 24-25% in a few years, with corporate overheads held at sub 5-6% of revenue for FY30.

risks_watch: Commission regulation: a forthcoming discussion paper could change commission structures and PoSP classification, which the company has not yet seen.
Base effects: FY27 H2 faces a high base after the strong FY26 growth; Q4 seasonality means profitability is concentrated in the March quarter.
Reliance on the PoSP network: DP productivity, retention and recruitment must keep rising for premium growth.
Disclosure limits: no segment split of GI motor vs health, no renewal premium, no new vs renewal margins; management asked for more time.
Exceptional item of INR 55 crores (non-cash, preference share conversion) recorded in the nine months to December 2025; ESOP cost of INR 25 crores (2.3% of revenue) is expected to fall by FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident and data-led on profitability milestones and operating leverage, but deliberately non-committal on numbers: no formal guidance, and segment and renewal-premium splits were withheld. Answers on regulation and PoSP classification were speculative.
key_quotes: Q4 became our first profitable quarter. It just demonstrated the fact that there is operating leverage and with scale and expanding service EBITDA, there is significant high profitability to come.

Our growth strategy is anchored in our ability to recruit individuals at scale, seamlessly onboard them onto our Turtlemint Pro platform, handhold them in their training, give them skills and tools to get activated.
The platform has the ability to absorb any volatility, and it is able to pass down any cost structure, any commercial structure changes.
Service EBITDA is our measure of profitability after accounting for all the variable cost of our business.
